# Engclaw

> Engclaw is a free, open-source desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) for practising English pronunciation. It scores a spoken sentence phone by phone against a reference, shows which sounds, words and intonation to fix, and runs entirely on the user's computer with no account, server or telemetry.

Key facts:
- License: GPL-3.0-or-later. Price: free.
- Platforms: macOS Apple Silicon (.dmg), Windows x64 (.exe), Linux x64 (AppImage, .deb). Intel Macs are not supported.
- Score out of 100 = 30% acoustic similarity (dynamic time warping against a Kokoro reference voice) + 40% correct sounds (phoneme error rate) + 30% correct words (word error rate).
- Local models (Apache-2.0, downloaded once from Hugging Face, ~2.6 GB total): wav2vec2-lv-60-espeak-cv-ft (phone recognition), wav2vec2-large-960h (speech recognition), Kokoro-82M (reference voice).
- Features: Practice, Shadowing (YouTube + dictation), Pronunciation game, Dictionary (IPA, roots, animated mouth and tongue), optional Converse AI speaking partner.
- Scoring is English only; the interface is English and Vietnamese.
- Privacy: recordings, history and settings stay in the local app data folder. Network is used only for model download, YouTube, word illustrations, update checks and a user-configured AI provider.
